subject: RFI: Isolated service-mesh segmentation & physical operator controls
messages:
From: Daniel Hill <daniel.hill@novapulse.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: lindsey.park@novapulse.com, security-ops@novapulse.com
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI items — isolated network & operator access (follow-up)

Tessa — thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we consolidate answers for our security review board, could you clarify a few items where we need explicit policy or evidence? High level asks below — we can iterate but please flag anything that requires legal or procurement: 

1) Network isolation: do you support a hardened service-mesh inside the VPC that enforces egress-deny-by-default and per-workload L7 allow rules? If so, can you provide a segmentation matrix showing which Redwood services initiate egress during on-prem operations (control plane callbacks, telemetry, license checks)?

2) Physical operator controls: for on-prem/appliance installs, what operator tasks require console/SSH access vs an operator jumpbox? Do you provide an operator runbook and an auditable checklist for patch windows?

3) Maintenance and patching: what's your recommended maintenance cadence for kernel and runtime patches for an air-gapped deployment and how do you deliver signed patch packages for customers who cannot reach the public internet?

4) Evidence: we need artifacts (runbook, network matrix, sample NetworkPolicy, and any KMS integration statements) to include in our RFP pack.

Appreciate concise bullets where possible — Lindsey and their security ops team will review.

—Daniel
Security Engineering, NovaPulse Health
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Hill <daniel.hill@novapulse.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI items — isolated network & operator access (follow-up)

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Attached are the three artifacts you asked for and short answers below. If you want a single consolidated PDF for the board, we can produce one by EOD Friday.

Attachments: network-segmentation-matrix.xlsx; operator-access-runbook-v1.pdf; sample-k8s-networkpolicy.yaml.txt

Short answers (high level):
- Network isolation: Yes. Redwood’s Private deployment ships with a default egress-deny posture enforced at the service-mesh layer plus per-workload L7 policies. We recommend combining our mesh rules with VPC route tables for defense-in-depth. The attached matrix enumerates control-plane endpoints, optional telemetry destinations, and the minimum egress ports/protocols required.
- Physical operator controls: Operator tasks are classified as (1) local console-only (operator on-site console for hardware diagnostics), (2) jumpbox-mediated admin (for orchestration/ops via bastion), and (3) unattended automated jobs (patching, backups). The runbook includes a checklist for operator sign-in/out, MFA on jumpboxes, and a recorded attestation step for patch windows.
- Maintenance/patching for air-gapped: We publish signed patch bundles (PGP-signed tarballs) and an offline patching tool. For air-gapped customers we deliver packages via SFTP, signed USB, or partner courier depending on contractual terms. Recommended cadence: quarterly runtime patches, monthly critical security hotfixes as required.

I've copied Marissa and Irene to add specifics on operator credentialing and evidence artifacts.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 04 Apr 2029 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI items — isolated network & operator access (follow-up)

Daniel — adding the operational controls details you requested:

- Operator access model: we require a bastion/jumpbox for any remote administrative actions. Local console access is allowed only for hardware maintenance windows and must be logged via an operator attestation in the runbook (signed by the facility manager).
- Least privilege: Administrative roles are split into: Operator (hardware, power-cycling), Platform Admin (orchestration, upgrades), and Security Auditor (read-only access to telemetry). Role separation is enforced through RBAC in the control plane and via short-lived certificates for jumpbox sessions.
- Audit trail: All operator sessions (local or jumpbox) are logged; jumpbox sessions stream session metadata to the local telemetry collector and to the customer’s SIEM endpoint (if configured). The runbook contains sample audit entries and required evidence fields.
- Emergency access: We support an emergency break-glass procedure that requires two-person authorization and a tamper-evident operator log (template in the runbook).

Attachment note: the operator-access-runbook-v1.pdf contains the templates and the evidence checklist you can feed into your RFP binder.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFI items — isolated network & operator access (follow-up)

Quick technical supplement — sample NetworkPolicy and control-plane egress list (excerpt):

- Control-plane egress: minimal set: license.redwood.ai:443 (optional, only for hosted telemetry), time.redwood.ai:123 (NTP), internal-kv-sync.local:7000 (cluster-local, no external egress required when air-gapped). The attached matrix enumerates ports by service.

- Sample NetworkPolicy snippet (attached as sample-k8s-networkpolicy.yaml.txt) is intended as a starting point for whitelist rules. For air-gapped installs replace external hostnames with internal IP aliases and use the provided offline CA for certs.

- KMS integration: we support KMS bindings to customer HSMs via PKCS#11 and KMIP. When operating fully air-gapped, keys can be injected during install and rotated via offline token exchange; the runbook has the rotation playbook.

—Ben
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Team — this is extremely helpful, thank you. Received the three attachments and the short answers are clear. A couple of small follow-ups before we lock the RFP pack: 

1) Can you add an explicit line in the Network Segmentation Matrix that says "no default egress to public internet in air-gapped mode"? We need that explicit statement for procurement.
2) Please confirm whether the runbook's emergency break-glass requires one or two on-call sign-offs for operator-initiated local console sessions (your note said two-person authorization for break-glass — we want that reflected in the evidence template).

If you can send those two clarifications as a quick addendum we can close the RFP and move to SOW. Will loop procurement next.

—Daniel
Security Engineering, NovaPulse Health
